knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}?
$$

I. $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0$

II. $A$ is not invertible

III. $\text{rank}(A)=5$

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1\ne 0.
$$

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{dim(Null}(A))\ne 0,$ then according to the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix $A$ can't be invertible.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is not invertible, then by the invertible matrix theorem, we must have $\text{rank}(A)\ne 5.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{\begin{bmatrix}-3{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}?
$$

I. $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0$

II. $A$ is not invertible

III. $\text{rank}(A)=5$

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1\ne 0.
$$

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{dim(Null}(A))\ne 0,$ then according to the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix $A$ can't be invertible.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is not invertible, then by the invertible matrix theorem, we must have $\text{rank}(A)\ne 5.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{\begin{bmatrix}-3{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}?
$$

I. $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0$

II. $A$ is not invertible

III. $\text{rank}(A)=5$

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1\ne 0.
$$

- Statement II is true. Since $\text{dim(Null}(A))\ne 0,$ then according to the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix $A$ can't be invertible.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is not invertible, then by the invertible matrix theorem, we must have $\text{rank}(A)\ne 5.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and  $det(A)=1?$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $A$ is invertible

- **II.** $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}$

- **III.** $\text{nullity}(A)=5$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is true. Indeed,   a matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=1\ne 0,$ our matrix $A$ must be  invertible.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}.$

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is invertible,  it must be $\text{nullity}(A)=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and  $det(A)=4?$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $A$ is invertible

- **II.** $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}$

- **III.** $\text{nullity}(A)=3$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=3=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is true. Indeed,   a matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=4\ne 0,$ our matrix $A$ must be  invertible.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}.$

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is invertible,  it must be $\text{nullity}(A)=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and  $det(A)=2?$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $A$ is invertible

- **II.** $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}$

- **III.** $\text{nullity}(A)=3$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=3=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is true. Indeed,   a matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=2\ne 0,$ our matrix $A$ must be  invertible.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}.$

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is invertible,  it must be $\text{nullity}(A)=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and  $det(A)=-3?$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $A$ is invertible

- **II.** $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}$

- **III.** $\text{nullity}(A)=3$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=3=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is true. Indeed,   a matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=-3\ne 0,$ our matrix $A$ must be  invertible.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}.$

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is invertible,  it must be $\text{nullity}(A)=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)={\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R}?
$$
- **I.** $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0$
- **II.** $A$ is  invertible
- **III.** $\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{5}$

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)={0} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)={{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R}
$$

we conclude that 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=2\ne 0.
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $\text{dim(Null}(A))\ne 0,$ then according to the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix $A$ can't be invertible.

- Statement III is true. Since $A$ is not invertible, then by the invertible matrix theorem, we must have $\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{5}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)={\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R}?
$$
- **I.** $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0$
- **II.** $A$ is  invertible
- **III.** $\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{5}$

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)={0} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)={{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R}
$$

we conclude that 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=2\ne 0.
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $\text{dim(Null}(A))\ne 0,$ then according to the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix $A$ can't be invertible.

- Statement III is true. Since $A$ is not invertible, then by the invertible matrix theorem, we must have $\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{5}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{\begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R\}?
$$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $\text{dim(Null}(A))=1$

- **II.** $A$ is invertible

- **III.** $\text{rank}(A)<4$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{4} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=4=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Indeed, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $\text{dim(Null}(A))\ne 0,$ then according to the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix $A$ can't be invertible.

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $A$ is not invertible, then by the invertible matrix theorem, we must have $\text{rank}(A)\ne 4,$ or equivalently $\text{rank}(A)<4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and  $det(A)=-1?$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $A$ is not invertible

- **II.** $\text{rank}(A)=3$

- **III.** $A$ has $4$ pivot columns
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{4} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=4=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is false. Indeed,   a matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=-1\ne 0,$ our matrix $A$ must be  invertible.

- Statement II is false. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{rank}(A)=4.$

- Statement III is true. Since $\text{rank}(A)=4$,  it must be $\text{dim(Col}(A))=4$ which, in turn, means that  $A$ has $4$ pivot columns.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and  $det(A)=-3?$

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $A$ is not invertible

- **II.** $\text{rank}(A)=3$

- **III.** $A$ has $4$ pivot columns
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{4} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=4=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is false. Indeed,   a matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=-3\ne 0,$ our matrix $A$ must be  invertible.

- Statement II is false. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{rank}(A)=4.$

- Statement III is true. Since $\text{rank}(A)=4$,  it must be $\text{dim(Col}(A))=4$ which, in turn, means that  $A$ has $4$ pivot columns.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $7\times 7$ matrix and  $\text{rank}(A)=7?$ 

I. $A$ is invertible

II. $\text{Col}(A)=\{0\}$

III. $\text{nullity}(A)=0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $7\times 7$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{7} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=7=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is true. By the invertible matrix theorem,  $A$ is an invertible matrix because $\text{rank}(A)=7.$

- Statement II is false. Since $A$ is invertible, it must be $\text{Col}(A)={R}^{7}.$

- Statement III is true. By the invertible matrix theorem, we have $\text{nullity}(A)=0$ because $A$ is invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is, "I and III only."

knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and  $det(A)=0?$ 

I. $A$ is not invertible

II. $\text{rank}(A)\ne 5$

III. $\text{Null}(A)=\{0\}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{5} \\  & \text{dim(Col)}(A)=5=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null)}(A)=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn. 

- Statement I is true. A matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if $det(A)\ne 0.$ Since here we have $det(A)=0,$ our matrix $A$ is not invertible.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, by the invertible matrix theorem
$A$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\text{rank}(A)=5.$
Since $A$ is not invertible, we must have $\text{rank}(A)\ne 5.$

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is not invertible,  it must be $\text{Null}(A)\ne \{0\}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
